key_insight: The paper turns finite-time Lyapunov bounds for an associated SDE into convergence-rate guarantees for stochastic gradient algorithms via a rate-transfer method.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a calculus-based route to prove or estimate optimization rates for new SGD-style methods without doing a full discrete-time analysis from scratch.
method: Construct an SDE that approximates or corresponds to the stochastic gradient algorithm.
Prove a finite-time Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE using smoothness and moment assumptions.
Transfer the SDE bound into a finite-time convergence rate for the discrete algorithm.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and extends to new algorithms through calculus arguments.
watch_item: The approach depends on generic moment and smoothness conditions plus a valid SDE connection, so it may be less straightforward for highly non-smooth or strongly non-asymptotic implementations.
paper_title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
